nrIncident.message:
A power cut at Kentish Town station means no trains can call at this station. As a result, trains running through this station will run non stop.
Disruption is expected until approximately 07:00.
Customer advice:
If you are travelling to or from Kentish Town, you will need to use London Underground services to complete your journey, as Thameslink trains are currently unable to call at the station.
Due to a local power cut, Thameslink services are running through Kentish Town without stopping in either direction. Please allow up to an extra 15 to 20 minutes to complete your journey via alternative routes.
Alternative travel advice:
Travelling to Kentish Town: If you are travelling southbound, please remain on your train to London St Pancras International; if you are travelling northbound, please alight at London St Pancras International. From there, walk across to Kings Cross St Pancras Underground station to take a Northern line (High Barnet / Mill Hill East branch) train to Kentish Town.
Travelling from Kentish Town: Take a southbound London Underground Northern line service to Kings Cross St Pancras, then walk across to London St Pancras International to join an onward Thameslink train to your destination.
Ticket acceptance:
To complete your journey you can use your ticket on the following at no extra cost
• Any alternative Thameslink service to / from London St Pancras International
• London Underground Northern line services between Kentish Town and London St Pancras International
Planning your journey:
For help planning your journey, check live departure boards, view a live network map or see alternative route guides.
If you’re travelling within London, you can use the TfL Journey Planner.
Can you tell me more about the incident?
A power cut at Kentish Town means that the station lights are not working. As the station is in darkness, it's not safe for trains to call.
Station teams and the local electricity suppliers are working to ensure that the station is returned to a mains electricity supply as quickly as possible.
Check before you travel:
You can check your journey using the National Rail real-time Journey Planner.
Compensation:
You may be entitled to compensation if you experience a delay in completing your journey today. Please keep your train ticket and make a note of your journey, as both will be required to support any claim.

nrIncident.summary: No trains between Swanley and Otford: disruption expected until 15:30
nrIncident.routes:
Southeastern between London Victoria and Maidstone East, and also between London Charing Cross and Ashford International
Thameslink between London Blackfriars and Sevenoaks
nrIncident.message:
A fault with the signalling system between Swanley and Otford means that all lines are blocked. As a result, trains running between these stations may be cancelled, delayed or revised.
Disruption is expected until 15:30.
Southeastern customer advice:
What's happened?
A fault with the signalling system has been reported in the Swanley area. As a result, all lines are blocked between Swanley and Otford.
Response staff are on site and have identified an issue with a set of points; they are hopeful the issue should be rectified by 14:40.
How does this affect my journey?
Services are currently unable to run between Swanley and Otford. This affects services between London and Maidstone East, and Thameslink services to / from Sevenoaks.
Services running between London Victoria / London Charing Cross and Maidstone East / Ashford International will be diverted to run via Tonbridge.
What should I do?
You can use your ticket at no extra cost on Stagecoach route 510 between Maidstone and Ashford.
Alternative routes:
For details of alternative routes that may be available to complete your journey, please refer to our Alternative routes during disruption maps.
How can I stay up to date?
You can follow Southeastern on Twitter (X) @SE_Railway or follow the Southeastern WhatsApp channel.
Thameslink customer advice:
You will need to use an alternative route to travel and allow at least 30 minutes extra time to complete your journey.
Thameslink trains that normally run to Sevenoaks will be diverted after Bickley to run via Petts Wood and Orpington to Sevenoaks. Services towards London will run via the same route from Sevenoaks.
The following stations will not be served until further notice:
• St Mary Cray
• Swanley
• Eynsford
• Shoreham
• Otford
• Bat & Ball
Alternative travel options are being organised and you will be able to find further information here as soon as those have been confirmed.
Please talk to station staff, look at information boards or check your journey planner for the latest information.
Planning your journey:
For help planning your journey, check live departure boards, view a live network map or see alternative route guides.
If you’re travelling within London, you can use the TfL Journey Planner.
Stay up to date on the move with Southern’s WhatsApp channel. Live updates are available Monday to Friday, 07:00–21:00.
Can you tell me more about the incident?
A points failure has been reported, and this is preventing trains from using some of the routes through this area.
Points are movable sections of track that allow trains to change routes at junctions. If they develop a fault, they may not move into the correct position or the signalling system may be unable to confirm they are securely positioned. Sometimes, points can be secured in one position to allow some trains to continue.
Network Rail signalling specialists are investigating the fault and working to restore services. Repairs may involve removing an obstruction, fixing the equipment or replacing faulty parts. It may not be possible to confirm how long the disruption will last until the cause is identified.

You can check your journey using the National Rail real-time Journey Planner.
For helpful advice if you need to travel on a rail replacement service, including accessibility and bicycle information, please use our Rail Replacement Services page.

Please be advised that replacement vehicles may be busier than usual, and you should allow extra time for your journey.

You may be entitled to compensation if you experience a delay in completing your journey today. Please keep your train ticket and make a note of your journey, as both will be required to support any claim.
